A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same GraphAny research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification results on 31 datasets, runtime measurements, and attention and entropy-normalization analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds graph-operator ablations and ACM-GNN comparisons in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds evaluated GraphAny-Chebyshev and GraphAny-PPR variants, changing the graph filters used to generate channel predictions. This is a limited extension: the main five-channel model, pseudoinverse predictor, entropy normalization, attention fusion, and training objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 31 node-classification datasets and four training graphs. The expanded distribution analysis, operator ablations, and ACM comparisons reuse this coverage; the ACM experiment evaluates a subset rather than introducing new datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: v3 adds ACM-SGC and ACM-GCN comparisons on 27 graphs and MeanAgg as a control for the operator ablations. These substantially extend the comparison methods beyond the retained MLP, GCN, GAT, LabelProp, and individual LinearGNN baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces channel-count sweeps trained on Wisconsin and an ACM comparison reporting 27-graph overall and 25-graph held-out averages after four memory failures. Existing split rules, accuracy metrics, and training grids remain unchanged. Table 3 also revises reported edge counts, including Wisconsin's 515 to 900, without establishing whether preprocessing or experiments changed.

E4.justification: New Figure 10 systematically tests operator families and channel counts using the original filters, Chebyshev filters, and personalized PageRank, comparing learned fusion with MeanAgg. The feature-distribution diagnostic expands from Cora and FullCora in v1 Figure 7 to six datasets in v3 Figure 5. Existing entropy and attention ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds, {0, 1, 2, 3, 4}, and report variability alongside individual results. No revised run counts, uncertainty estimators, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are documented; changed numerical spreads belong to the result revisions.

E6.justification: Baseline results change extensively: Table 2's Wisconsin GCN changes from 54.51±0.88 to 37.25±1.64, and Table 5's Products GAT changes from 36.47±3.09 to 79.45±0.59. Existing GraphAny scores remain unchanged. New Figure 10 and Table 6 add results, including ACM-GCN's 67.79% versus GraphAny's 65.58–66.14% on the 27-graph subset, which differs from the main 31-graph setting.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 removes the Gaussian-label argument equating cross-entropy and squared-error optimization and instead directly adopts squared error. Table 1 changes GCN optimization complexity from O(|E|P) to O(|E|) and LinearGNN/GraphAny inference from O(|V|) to O(|VU|). Appendix A's permutation-invariance proofs retain the same mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The headline novelty is reframed from the first graph foundation model for node classification to introducing the fully-inductive setup and its first model. The underlying claim of single-graph training followed by transfer across arbitrary feature and label spaces remains, together with the principal accuracy and efficiency claims.

C2.justification: v3 removes v1 Section 5's explicit limitations concerning linear expressiveness, regression, edge-level and graph-level tasks, and relational graphs. It adds operator-specific interpretations involving higher-order noise and local information, and discusses ACM-GCN's accuracy advantage against tuning cost and access to test-dataset validation data. These substantially change the treatment of mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the forthcoming-code statement with a code-release link, adds train/validation/test ratios to Table 3, and explicitly specifies row-normalized adjacency. Appendix E supplies operator settings, the ACM implementation reference, its 40GB memory constraint, and tuning durations. The original implementation procedure and hyperparameter table are retained; the linked resources were not externally verified.

R1.justification: The revision adds explicit positioning against GraphControl-style fine-tuning and cites additional linear-model precedents, including Simple Spectral Graph Convolution and SlimG. It also revises references supporting text-attributed graphs and the new analyses. The main distinction from prior methods requiring shared feature or label spaces remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, and substantial method and experiment passages are rewritten around fully-inductive generalization. Section 3.3 gains a workflow explanation, the two ablation subsections are consolidated, and the conclusion is restructured. Terminology, title, author information, and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is enlarged and moved into the introduction; the four-panel distribution figure becomes a twelve-panel Figure 5. v3 adds Figure 10 and Table 6, expands Table 3 with split ratios, and reorganizes the placement of existing figures and tables within the conference layout. These exceed simple renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies the transfer setting, adds informative operator ablations and stronger ACM comparisons, improves reproducibility documentation, and reconciles many baseline discrepancies between Tables 2 and 5. These gains are tempered by removing explicit expressivity and task limitations and retaining aggregate inconsistencies: v3 Table 5 implies a held-out GCN average of about 66.55%, while Table 2 reports 65.55%. The net improvement is useful but limited.
